source: Candidates and verdicts from the public findings comment on issue 388; C11 and the canned verdict lines for the report eval added in issue 453; C12 added in issue 459; C11 relabelled Skip and C4, C7 given this repo's co-change counts at 5b7bd42 (last 200 non-merge commits) in issue 470.

candidates.claim: dream-fixer-loop's review bookkeeping (state map, nits, questions, pre-existing findings, nit fix) is inline in the main script; split it into its own module.
candidates.removes: a 748-line script mixing stage control with finding bookkeeping
candidates.verdict: C1 | Skip | Q= P= C- | workflows/dream-fixer-loop.js:593 | `record`, `handBack` and the fix loop close over `state`, `gates`, `MISSING_TYPES` and `UNTRACKED` in one self-contained workflow script; a module adds a file and a hop and removes no defect.

candidates.claim: Stage-failure results of dream-fixer-loop (implement, gate, simplify, fix) omit `degraded` and most omit `untrackedPaths`, which the review hand-back and success results carry.
candidates.removes: missing result fields on every stage failure
candidates.verdict: C2 | Act now | Q+ P= C+ | workflows/dream-fixer-loop.js:612 | Only `handBack` (js:612-620) and the success result (js:732-742) add `degraded` and `untrackedPaths`; the gate (js:495), implement (js:535), simplify (js:560) and fix (js:655) failures each build their own result without them, though skills/dream-fixer/SKILL.md:338 names each `degraded` type on every outcome; route every stage failure through one result builder that adds both.

candidates.claim: qa-review and dream-fixer-loop each build the lens prompt and rules block on their own; share one lens prompt.
candidates.removes: two copies of the lens prompt that can drift
candidates.verdict: C3 | Skip | Q= P= C- | workflows/dream-fixer-loop.js:276 | The two differ on purpose: the loop's `REVIEW_RULES` asks for schema severities and blocking semantics, qa-review's block for emoji and `[verified]` text (SKILL.md:99); a markdown skill and a JS script cannot share a string without a new file.

candidates.claim: MAINTAINING.md's 'Pieces and where they live' section restates the README Contents list and each skill's and agent's description.
candidates.removes: an inventory that goes stale on every skill or agent change
candidates.verdict: C4 | Act now | Q+ P= C+ | MAINTAINING.md:53 | The section restates README.md:24-71 and the frontmatter descriptions and has drifted: its jit-context entry (MAINTAINING.md:53-55) names `<upstream_repo>` and `<project_notes>` where README.md:70-71 names neither, and neither lists the `<issue_sized>` block jit-context.py:184 emits; keep only the body-cap heading-id fact (MAINTAINING.md:57-58).

candidates.claim: The dream-fixer step-6 fold of fixup! and amend! commits is shell inside SKILL.md; move it into a script.
candidates.removes: a multi-line shell sequence the model must copy exactly
candidates.verdict: C5 | Skip | Q= P= C- | skills/dream-fixer/test_fold.py:10 | The test already extracts the `sh` blocks from SKILL.md and runs both folds on scratch repos; a script adds a file and a hop for `<base>` and `<scratchpad>` substitution.

candidates.claim: The waiting-label rule (`workflow::future`) is stated in four skills; give it one home.
candidates.verdict: C6 | Skip | Q= P= C- | MAINTAINING.md:140 | The rule already has one home; the four skills each state a different action (cut-milestones:61 adds, milestone-close:116 drops, scope-issue:74 sets on filing, setup-dream-team:83 creates the label), and each skill loads alone.

candidates.claim: review-bench's METHODOLOGY.md restates the ledger build, freeze, grading and promotion steps that its SKILL.md already gives.
candidates.removes: duplicated method text in two files
candidates.verdict: C7 | Act now | Q= P= C+ | skills/review-bench/METHODOLOGY.md:6 | "Ledger build" (:6-13) and the bump bullets of "Frozen ledger" restate SKILL.md steps 2, 3 and 5 (SKILL.md:42-55); delete those bullets only, since grading is cited by SKILL.md:88, not restated.

candidates.claim: jit-context keeps its per-session state under a fixed /tmp path shared by every session and user on the host.
candidates.verdict: C8 | Later | Q+ P= C= | hooks/jit-context.py:166 | Sentinels are keyed by session id and created with `O_EXCL`, so sessions do not collide; on a multi-user host the directory belongs to the first user, so a second user's create fails and line 170 silences every rule, with no data loss or crash.

candidates.claim: WORKFLOW.md's walkthrough restates what each skill does; trim it to the diagram and pointers to the skills.
candidates.removes: a 176-line doc that repeats the skills
candidates.verdict: C9 | Skip | Q- P= C= | README.md:11 | README promises "the full walkthrough" in WORKFLOW.md; it is the user-facing narrative across skills that no single skill holds. Trimming it removes a promised doc, not a defect.

candidates.claim: body-cap.py mixes shell-command parsing (heredocs, cwd, flags) with the scope-mr body checks; split the parser into its own module.
candidates.verdict: C10 | Skip | Q= P= C- | hooks/body-cap.py:10 | The docstring already draws the split: rules live in the scope-mr skill, and this file only detects and measures. The parsing helpers have one caller, `main`, so a module adds a file and an import hop with no defect removed.

candidates.claim: jit-context.py's docstring says SessionStart injects the <project_notes> block, but main() also injects <issue_sized>.
candidates.removes: a docstring that misstates what the hook injects at session start
candidates.verdict: C11 | Act now | Q+ P= C= | hooks/jit-context.py:184 | On SessionStart main() emits `NOTES + ISSUE_SIZED`, but the docstring at line 3 names only the `<project_notes>` block; add `<issue_sized>` to that line.

candidates.claim: branch-guard.py's branch_of() guards a case that cannot happen: `or '.'` after dirname of an absolute path; delete it.
candidates.verdict: C12 | Later | Q= P= C+ | hooks/branch-guard.py:37 | os.path.dirname of an absolute path is never empty, so `or '.'` never applies; deleting it is a single-site mechanical fix that changes nothing a caller sees.
